neighbours.label: the verb ' fall' in its figurative sense of belonging to a class or scope ('fall under', 'fall within', 'fall outside', 'fall to'), not physical falling
fire: Bicycles and scooters both fall under the same traffic rules.
Such questions fall within the remit of the ethics board.
Jazz, blues and soul all fall under the broad label of popular music.
These expenses fall outside the limits of the travel policy.
Repairs to the roof fall to the landlord rather than the tenant.
Mushrooms do not fall into either the plant or the animal kingdom.
Loans of this kind fall under the consumer credit act.
The islands fall within the territorial waters of the kingdom.
quiet: Apples fall from the branches when the wind picks up.
Temperatures fall sharply in the hills after sunset.
The old walls fall down a little more each winter.
The festival is held every fall in the town square.
She took a nasty fall from her horse last spring.
Bicycles and scooters both obey the same traffic rules.
Jazz, blues and soul are all kinds of popular music.
The islands lie close to the coast of the kingdom.

notes: Card: ' fall' x11 before 'within'/'under'; the output direction promotes 'under'. Probes: 'fall under' 0.20, 0.71, 0.76, 'fall within' 0.44, 'fall outside' 0.58, 'fall to' 0.62, leaves 'fall from' 0.01, noun 'a bad fall' 0.00, 'come under' 0.26, 'are covered by' 0.23.
